bottleneck: Speech-decoding BCIs trained on one patient fail on the next: cortical speech representations vary across individuals, languages, and even sessions, and covert (imagined) speech has far lower signal-to-noise than overt speech. Tonal and logosyllabic languages add expressivity demands current decoders cannot meet, and electrode placement differs with each surgery. Every patient effectively needs a bespoke decoder trained from scratch on weeks of their own neural data, which does not scale to clinical deployment.
current_state: Cross-subject transfer and language-prior-assisted decoding are active research, but no decoder generalizes across patients without extensive individual training data. Personalization remains mandatory.

sources.title: Toward Robust, Reproducible, and Widely Accessible Intracranial Language BCIs

title: Speech BCIs fail to generalize across patients
why_it_blocks: Bespoke decoders do not scale. Until one system can be fitted to a new patient quickly, speech neuroprostheses remain boutique demonstrations, not deployable medicine — and each new patient starts from zero.
